mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is always interpreted as a bullish signal for the S&P 500, leading to positive 20-day returns. This is based on the historical correlation between low interest rates and equity market performance, and we are using the current low rate as evidence for the always-on signal.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market stress condition (UNRATE > 7.5%) indicates high unemployment and weak economic activity, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors flee to safety. The signal is activated when unemployment rises above 7.5%.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when UNRATE > 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint occurrence of a supply chain contraction (INDPRO < 98.5) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.5%) indicates a severe economic downturn, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is activated when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO < 98.5 AND UNRATE > 7.5.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations and reduce liquidity, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is activated when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 900,000 units) indicates weakening consumer demand and potential recession, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is activated when housing starts fall below 900,000 units.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST < 900.

mechanism_narrative: The joint occurrence of low consumer spending (RSAFS < 420,000 million dollars) and low housing starts (HOUST < 900,000 units) signals a weak economy, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is activated when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when RSAFS < 420000 AND HOUST < 900.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 98.5) indicates weakening economic activity, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is activated when industrial production falls below 98.5.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO < 98.5.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2%), strong economic growth supports corporate earnings and leads to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is activated when the annualized GDP growth rate exceeds 2%.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2%.
